original_question: (N. Brady). Do there exist finitely presented subgroups of right-angled Artin groups whose Dehn functions are super-exponential, or sub-exponential but not polynomial? Such subgroups are known to exist in general CAT(0) groups, whereas the only Dehn functions currently realized for subgroups of right-angled Artin groups are exponential and polynomial of arbitrary degree.
target_in_paper: Problem 21.126 (N. Brady) in the “New Problems (21st issue, 2026)” portion of Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook.
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the official problem essentially verbatim: it asks whether finitely presented subgroups of right-angled Artin groups can have Dehn functions that are either super-exponential or strictly between polynomial and exponential. The accompanying motivation in your draft also matches the paper’s adjacent comment: such behavior is known in general CAT(0) groups, while the realized Dehn functions for subgroups of right-angled Artin groups are currently exponential and polynomial of arbitrary degree.
missing_details: The existence quantifier is over some ambient right-angled Artin group A and some finitely presented subgroup H ≤ A.
The Dehn function is the Dehn function of the subgroup H as a finitely presented group, understood up to the usual equivalence relation for Dehn functions.
The phrases “super-exponential” and “sub-exponential but not polynomial” should be read as statements about the growth class of that Dehn function, not about one specific presentation.
The CAT(0)-group comparison and the list of currently realized growth types are contextual remarks from the paper, not extra hypotheses of the question.
refined_question: Does there exist a finitely presented subgroup H ≤ A of some right-angled Artin group A whose Dehn function δ_H, considered up to the standard equivalence of Dehn functions, is either super-exponential, or else sub-exponential but not equivalent to any polynomial?
justification: For arXiv:1401.0300, the nearest official formulation is the standalone open problem labeled 21.126. Your draft is already very close to that exact statement, and even its explanatory sentence tracks the paper’s own comment. Because the notebook entry is intentionally brief, the only sharpening needed to make the question fully stand-alone is to spell out the ambient-group quantifier H ≤ A and the standard convention that Dehn-function growth is considered up to Dehn-function equivalence. The paper does not add further hypotheses or supply an explicit equivalent reformulation.
